correctness.rationale: For all integer n >= 3, cubicity makes complements of double total dominating sets exactly open packings. Direct enumeration of common-neighbor edges equals the square of the auxiliary two-regular graph; its components depend on the parity of n. Cyclic gap compositions prove every coefficient of the squared-cycle independence polynomial and the six residue counts. The standalone verifier separately checks direct labeling, complete conflict backtracking, graph edge identities, and coefficient maxima. Finite testing is corroboration only; the four-step general proof is complete.

value.rationale: The all-cardinality domination polynomial is a natural substantial strengthening of the earlier numeric prism invariant and supplies all optimal configurations and six sharp residue-class counting formulas. The parity-coupled common-neighbor graph turns the original two-layer cyclic domination constraints into independent selections on one or two squared cycles. This explicit structure is reusable for probabilistic sampling/counts of feasible configurations; the special value lies in the natural complete family and structural classification, not in computing an isolated small example.
